content.text: The Mistake Almost Every Creator Makes First

Many Zimbabwean digital sellers start their online stores without realizing that they are building their businesses on shaky ground, using payment solutions that can be shut down at any moment, leaving them without a way to receive payments or access their customer data. This mistake is often made due to a lack of knowledge about the infrastructure required to support international digital commerce, and a reliance on platforms that are not designed to support their specific needs.
Why This Keeps Happening Even to Experienced Sellers

Even experienced sellers can fall victim to this mistake, as they may have built their businesses on existing infrastructure that is not designed to support their needs. This can be due to a variety of factors, including a lack of awareness about new technologies and infrastructure options, or a reliance on existing relationships with payment processors. As a result, they may not realize that they are vulnerable to disruption until it is too late.
The Real Cost of Getting This Wrong

The cost of getting this wrong can be devastating, as sellers may find themselves facing financial isolation, loss of revenue, and even business closure. This can have a ripple effect on the entire economy, as small businesses and entrepreneurs are often the backbone of local communities. By building their businesses on shaky ground, sellers are putting not only their own livelihoods at risk, but also the livelihoods of their customers and employees.
Don't let payment solution restrictions hold you back from selling digital products internationally.
How to Build the Stack That Cannot Be Taken Down

The solution lies in building a sovereign digital commerce stack, one that is not dependent on any single platform or payment processor. This can be achieved by using open-source infrastructure tools, such as GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, and Supabase, which can be customized to meet the specific needs of the seller. By taking control of their own infrastructure, sellers can ensure that their businesses are secure, scalable, and resilient to disruption.
The Infrastructure Decision That Changes Everything

The key to building a successful digital commerce business is to make the infrastructure decision that changes everything. This means choosing a payment processor that is not restricted, such as NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and has no fees for buyers. By making this decision, sellers can ensure that their customers can pay in their preferred currency, and that they can receive payments without any restrictions.
How can creators in Africa sell digital products to international buyers?

Global access through sovereign infrastructure works because every layer of the stack is geography-neutral by design. Cloudflare Pages serves your storefront from data centers close to your buyer — whether they are in London or Lagos, the page loads in under 200 milliseconds. NOWPayments generates a unique payment address for each transaction — the buyer sends crypto from any wallet, anywhere in the world. The blockchain confirms the transaction regardless of which country the sender is in. Your Cloudflare Worker receives the webhook and processes the order using the same logic for every buyer.
Choose a payment processor that is not restricted, such as NOWPayments, to ensure that your customers can pay in their preferred currency.

Use Supabase to manage your customer data. Configure your store to use a cryptocurrency that is widely accepted, such as USDT on Tron. Test your store to ensure that it is working correctly.
Frequently Asked Questions
How do I get started with building a sovereign digital commerce stack?

To get started, you'll need to choose a payment processor that is not restricted, such as NOWPayments. You'll also need to set up a hosting platform, such as GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, and configure your store to use a cryptocurrency that is widely accepted. You can find more information about how to do this in the Complete Builder Kit ($197), which includes all 6 blueprints and 7 templates you need to build, deploy, and scale a sovereign digital commerce stack.
What are the benefits of using a sovereign digital commerce stack?

The benefits of using a sovereign digital commerce stack include increased security, scalability, and resilience to disruption. By taking control of your own infrastructure, you can ensure that your business is secure, both from a technical and financial perspective. You'll also be able to accept payments from customers all over the world, without relying on any single platform or payment processor.
Can I still use my existing payment processor if I switch to a sovereign digital commerce stack?

In most cases, you can continue to use your existing payment processor, but you may need to configure it to work with your new infrastructure. It's always a good idea to check with your payment processor to see if they support the infrastructure you're planning to use. Additionally, you may want to consider switching to a payment processor that is more supportive of your needs, such as NOWPayments.
How do I know if my current payment solution is secure?

To determine if your current payment solution is secure, look for indicators such as a high level of encryption, regular security audits, and transparent communication about any potential security issues. You can also check to see if they support two-factor authentication, which adds an extra layer of security to your account. If you're unsure, it's always best to err on the side of caution and switch to a more secure solution.
What happens if I'm using a payment processor that gets shut down?

If you're using a payment processor that gets shut down, you'll need to switch to a new payment processor as soon as possible. This can be a challenging process, but it's essential to ensure that your business continues to operate smoothly. Make sure to choose a payment processor that is reliable, secure, and has a good reputation in the industry.
Can I use a single payment processor for all my digital commerce needs?

It's generally not recommended to use a single payment processor for all your digital commerce needs, as this can create a single point of failure. Instead, consider using a payment processor that supports multiple payment methods, such as NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and has no fees for buyers.
